title: Exact computation of quantum wave functions for nonlinear potentials
abstract: Recent work shows that the Schroedinger equation can be solved exactly based only on classical least action rspa.2025.0413. The computation is based on first solving a Hamilton-Jacobi equation for the action, computing the classical propagated density along all stationary action paths, and finally constructing the exact kernel and wave function based on these classical quantities alone. The method requires that the propagated classical square root density along each stationary action path is harmonic (where a sufficient condition is that the Laplacian of the propagated action is purely time-varying), as is the case for basic examples such as the double-slit, quantum tunneling, the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen experiment, or also as discussed here the relativistic propagator of a Higgs boson. This density is fundamentally different from using the Madelung density, which is the norm of an existing overall quantum wave.   In the case of arbitrary nonlinear potentials, this condition can still be verified without loss of generality, by using a harmonic coordinate transformation and an associated time scaling for the propagated classical density and quantum wave, as this paper details. The resulting quantum wave of the time-scaled Schroedinger equation is equivalent to the quantum wave of the original Schroedinger equation, extending a standard result of Duru and Kleinert. Hence, in principle it can replace the approximations of quantum perturbation theory.   For 1 to 3-dimensional systems, this harmonic coordinate change transforms a nonlinear potential into the quadratic potential of a linear oscillator, for which an exact analytic action and wave solution are already known. This makes the construction of the quantum wave beyond the hydrogen wave straightforward for basic cases where no exact solution has been derived, such as the quartic potential or the nonlinear pendulum.
summary: This paper details a novel, exact theoretical method to compute quantum wave functions for systems with nonlinear potentials. It achieves this by transforming the complex nonlinear Schrödinger equation into an equivalent, solvable linear harmonic oscillator problem using harmonic coordinate transformations and time scaling. This breakthrough allows for non-perturbative solutions for systems beyond the standard textbook examples.
main_problem: The paper addresses the exact computation of quantum wave functions for systems governed by nonlinear potentials, aiming to surpass the limitations of standard approximate methods like quantum perturbation theory.
main_result: The authors present a method that constructs the exact quantum wave function by transforming the nonlinear Schrödinger equation into a time-scaled, linear harmonic oscillator form via harmonic coordinate transformations.
method: The core method involves solving the Hamilton-Jacobi equation for the classical action, followed by applying a harmonic coordinate transformation and time scaling to map the problem onto a known solvable linear system.
model_or_system: The theory applies to quantum systems described by the Schrödinger equation, particularly those with nonlinear potentials (e.g., quartic potentials, nonlinear pendulums) or position-dependent inertia tensors.
key_observables: Action ($\varphi$), propagated classical density ($ho$), and the resulting quantum wave function ($\psi$).
important_parameters: The method is effective for 1 to 3-dimensional systems, where the transformation simplifies the potential to that of a linear oscillator.
main_assumptions: The method fundamentally requires that the propagated classical square root density remains harmonic throughout the transformation process.
figures_summary: The notes do not provide a summary of figures, but mention the derivation of the kernel $K(t', q')$ and the resulting eigenwaves $\psi_{kx,ky}$.
paper_structure: The paper builds from solving the Hamilton-Jacobi equation using least action paths, introduces the harmonic coordinate transformation and time scaling, proves the equivalence to the linear harmonic oscillator, and then applies this framework to solve specific nonlinear potentials.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, non-perturbative theoretical framework for finding exact solutions to quantum problems that are typically intractable, offering a rigorous alternative to semi-classical approximations.
